rationale: The formalization reproduces the static transform, RMS, factorization, K, alpha, indexing, and common-gamma structure reasonably well, with Fourier sign still unresolved. It is nevertheless not the paper's numerical theorem. Computed states and local errors are not generated by the modeled floating-point operations or mixed-radix FFT, while a supplied certificate assumes the local and intermediate estimates. Because epsilon is fixed before all coefficient witnesses, the O(epsilon) input condition and O(epsilon^2) remainder can absorb arbitrary finite discrepancies and have no uniform asymptotic content. The additional exact telescoping conjunct is already a run premise. Consequently neither implication direction holds, and the result is not-faithful-different rather than stronger.
